title: Scoped trace pivoting and log-joiner for multi-tenant structured ingest
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our current log ingestion fabric accepts structured JSON from multiple sources (edge proxies, runtime agents, client SDKs) but struggles to reliably correlate events across streams at scale in a multi-tenant environment. Engineers have been manually joining by trace_id and request_id downstream which increases query cost, delays root-cause analysis, and prevents low-latency alerting. Existing projects (ingest-normalizers, trace-linkers) partially overlap but do not provide a stable, low-latency pivot join service or a tenant-scoped normalization layer.
background: This task focuses on two coordinated pieces: (1) a small, horizontally scalable 'log-joiner' service that performs TTL-bound pivot joins across event streams (structured logs, trace spans, runtime KV cache events) using configurable pivot keys (trace_id, request_id, session_id), and (2) a scoped normalization transform that projects tenant-safe fields, enforces schema, and emits a canonical envelope consumed by downstream Loki/Elasticsearch adapters. The approach avoids monolithic re-ingestion by doing join/normalization at ingress with backpressure and dedupe semantics.
approach:
Design highlights:
- Pivot store: Redis cluster (tenant-sharded prefixing) with per-pivot TTL (default 30s), optional probabilistic bloom-based protection for very high-cardinality keys.
- Joiner logic: event arrives -> compute pivot keys -> write partial envelope to pivot store -> if matching envelope(s) present, emit joined record to normalized output stream (Kafka topic 'logs.normalized.v2') -> mark as emitted to avoid dupes.
- Tenant scoping: every pivot key prefixed by tenant_id, RBAC enforced at ingress.
- Schema normalization: use JSON schema registry and a lightweight WASM-based transformation chain to redact PII and map legacy fields to canonical names.
- Sink adapters: extend Loki producer to accept canonical labels (service, env, tenant, trace_span) and ES indexer with dynamic mappings; include label projection for fast Loki queries.
- Backpressure: Kafka producer acks and ingress will return 429 + Retry-After when pivot store/producer latency crosses thresholds.
- Feature gating: rollout behind ff :log-joiner-enabled and per-tenant opt-in.
- Observability: instrument join latency histogram, emit counter for joined vs partial emits, track pivot-store hit/miss ratio.
- Deployment: Kubernetes deployment in dedicated 'obs-ingest' k8s namespace, HPA by CPU and custom metric (pivot-store latency).
performance_targets:
- End-to-end additional join latency: p50 < 5ms, p95 < 25ms, p99 < 50ms under 2k rps for typical pivot size distributions.
- Pivot-store write/read 99th percentile < 10ms.
- Dedupe correctness: duplicate emission rate < 0.1% at steady state.
- Storage: expected Kafka normalized traffic increase ~15% (estimate validated by sampling).
migration_plan: 1) Implement joiner and normalization but default off. 2) Canary on internal tenant 'redwood-infra' (10% traffic) for 2 days, monitor errors and QPS. 3) Gradually expand to non-critical tenants with alerting thresholds. 4) Full rollout once 72-hour stability and no increase in missing-trace incidents. 5) Deprecate older downstream ad-hoc join jobs after 30 days of stable traffic.
acceptance_criteria:
- Normalized stream schema published and conforms to JSON schema registry.
- Logs from canary tenant show correct pivot correlation in dashboards (trace->log link flow).
- Icinga alerts: no increase in false positives; configured latency/failed-joins alerts firing only when thresholds breached.
- Integration tests that replay synthetic multi-stream traces validate correctness (includes duplicate and out-of-order arrivals).
- Production rollout documented and feature flagged.
- PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-ingest/pull/421
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Scoped+Trace+Pivot+Design
risks_and_mitigations:
- High-cardinality pivot keys can exhaust pivot-store: mitigate with tenant-level quotas and bloom filters; fallback to best-effort no-join path.
- Privacy/leakage risk when joining tenant data: mandatory tenant_id prefixing and schema redaction, and KMS-backed field masking for sensitive fields.
- Increased downstream traffic to Kafka/Loki/ES: capacity plan and autoscaling knobs; can disable joiner per-tenant if load spike.
- Backpressure propagation could surface to customers: tune Retry-After and make 429 transient; provide a telemetry endpoint with circuit-breaker status.
monitoring_and_alerts:
Dashboards to create/update:
- 'Log-Joiner Overview' (joined_rate, partial_rate, duplicate_rate, pivot_store_latency histogram)
- 'Tenant correlation health' (per-tenant joined_rate, failed_joins)
- Update existing latency/error dashboards to include trace-join hit ratio and percent of logs with trace_link.
Alerts:
- P1 if joined_rate drops >30% vs baseline for production tenants for 10m.
- P2 if pivot_store p99 latency >100ms for 5m.
- P3 if duplicate_rate >0.5% for 30m.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for pivot write/read, dedupe logic, schema transforms (in Go and WASM harness).
- Integration tests: local kafka+redis stack using testcontainers; replay recorded traffic with out-of-order arrival.
- Load tests: spike test to verify p99 latency and backpressure behavior; record resource usage.
- Run end-to-end QA run for 48h on canary tenant and verify dashboards and alert stability.
